Definition 24.3(Minimal same-scope first-response Hamiltonian predicate). The minimal same-
scope first-response Hamiltonian predicate is formallySameScopeQuantumSpatial1(H) and is ab-
breviated SSQ1(H). It holds iffH satisfies the following clauses.
(Q1) Hilbert internality:H is built only from the licensed projective-Hilbert and flat nonrelativistic
spatial projection.
(Q2) Declared domain:H acts on a declared dense domainD(H)⊂H.
(Q3) Self-adjointness: H is self-adjoint withD(H) =D(H∗) and Hψ=H∗ψfor allψ∈D(H),
or H is essentially self-adjoint on a declared core and its closure is the self-adjoint generator.
(Q4) Linearity: H is linear on the closed representative state space.
(Q5) Projective compatibility:H respects ray-level state identity and does not make global phase
standing-bearing.
(Q6) Locality:H is a local differential operator in the admitted spatial carrier.
(Q7) Spatial scalarity:H is scalar under lawful Euclidean spatial redescription and introduces no
preferred direction or anisotropic tensor.
(Q8) First-response order:H contains no spatial derivatives beyond the first nontrivial scalar
response, namely second order.
(Q9) Uniform principal response:the second-order principal symbol is proportional to the admitted
flat spatial metric and has no variable tensor coefficient unless declared richer scope.
(Q10) No hidden gauge connection:gauge potential terms are absent unless declared as connection
load.
(Q11) No hidden spin/internal operator:spin or internal-space matrices are absent unless declared.
(Q12) No relativistic mixing:no time-space symmetric relativistic operator, spinor projection, or
second-order time equation is imported.
(Q13) No nonlinear state dependence:no term depends onψ,|ψ|2, expectation values, or state
history unless declared effective/open scope.
(Q14) No open-system ledger:no bath, dissipative, Lindblad, or non-Hermitian sink/source term is
hidden inside the closed Hamiltonian.
(Q15) No measurement/update selector:no projection, collapse, record selection, or stochastic
update is included as same-scope closed generator content.
(Q16) No nonlocal operator:no fractional Laplacian, integral kernel, inverse operator, or memory
term is included.
(Q17) No undeclared boundary selector:boundary conditions and self-adjoint extensions are
anchors or external data unless fixed by the declared domain.

(Q18) Potential ledger discipline:a zeroth-order scalar term may enter only as declared scalar
potential/source ledgerV.
(Q19) Nontrivial spatial-response branch: the candidate is not merely a homogeneous phase
baseline for general spatial dynamics.
Remark 24.4(Target of the predicate). The predicateSSQ1 does not classify all possible quantum
theories. It classifies the minimal closed nonrelativistic first-response Hamiltonian class. A theory
outside SSQ1 may be legitimate as richer-scope, effective-scope, open-system, measurement/update,
relativistic, gauge, spin, or quantum-field structure, but it is not the theorem target.
Remark 24.5(The predicate is not definition by desired conclusion). The clauses ofSSQ1 are not
selected because they yield Schrödinger form. They are the target translation of closed autonomous
scalar nonrelativistic projective-Hilbert continuation. Removing Hilbert internality loses the carrier.
Removing self-adjoint domain discipline loses closed unitary continuation. Removing Euclidean
scalarity admits hidden vector/tensor backgrounds. Removing locality or first-response order admits
nonlocal or higher-response scope. Removing the no-update clauses admits measurement or open-
system repair. Every clause either preserves the declared target or marks a declared exit from
it.

25 Hamiltonian-response exhaustion
The predicate is narrow because the target is narrow. A broader predicate would not refute the
theorem; it would define a different theorem object by admitting additional anchors, operator load,
open/update ledgers, nonlocal structure, boundary data, or richer projection content.
Before the exhaustion proof begins, fix the comparator boundary. This argument is not canonical
quantization, not path integration, and not a Galilei-covariance derivation repackaged. Those
comparators operate after a quantum carrier and kinematic assumptions have already been admitted.

Remark 36.2(Scope of uniqueness). Uniqueness is uniqueness of form within the declared closed
autonomous scalar nonrelativistic projective-Hilbert projection envelope and up to declared scale
anchors ℏ,m, potential multiplication ledgerMV, and domain conditions. It is not uniqueness of all
quantum dynamics and not exclusion of declared richer-scope theories.
Corollary 36.3(Declared-domain extension). For a declared regular spatial domainQ⊆Rd, the
same local Hamiltonian form holds only relative to an explicit domain, boundary, and self-adjointness
certificate. Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, periodic, Friedrichs, deficiency-index, and other extension
selections are anchors of the declared domain problem, not hidden same-scope alternatives to the
primary full-space theorem.
